Paragraph: When I have been talking to you this way, what for do you not speak to me? One named Sugreeva, a virtuous and worthy one among monkeys, is expelled by his brother Vali, and he is roaming all over the world sorrowfully.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Hanuman is met with prolonged silence despite his extensive courteous speech, and grows mildly frustrated; he references Sugreeva's own painful exile and fraternal betrayal.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Hanuman voices his frustration honestly yet respectfully, and pivots to disclose Sugreeva's plight of being wronged and displaced by his own brother.
Outcome/Resolution: This prompts movement toward direct disclosure and eventual dialogue.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Relationship Challenges (Family): Fraternal betrayal and expulsion by Vali

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Adharma of fraternal betrayal (violation of bhratru-dharma)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Sugreeva's plight highlights the adharma of broken bhratru-dharma, sibling duty, causing deep sorrow and displacement.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Depicts grief and hopelessness stemming from family conflict and forced exile, and models assertive but respectful expression of one's own mild frustration.
